goal: Make `blit jobs retry` safely re-run exactly the files still failed at the end of a prior run, preserving raw filenames and `--ignore-existing` semantics.
recommended_approach: Persist a typed retry identity containing display text plus optional raw bytes, together with its terminal failure and incomplete-destination state, through summaries, RunRecord, log reconciliation, and FilterSpec; fold events across attempts by identity, then partition `--ignore-existing` retries without converting identities through the controller's native PathBuf.
comparison: The change correctly handles local terminal-state reconstruction, Unix raw names, and `--ignore-existing` partitioning, and the eight job-retry tests pass. It is not the best complete implementation because detached reconciliation still retains historical failures and Windows controllers discard raw identities. An independent guard for failure-then-FileCopied was red on the reviewed head and green after terminal-state removal; the worktree was restored cleanly to the reviewed SHA.
material_changes: Make detached LogRead reconciliation retain only terminal failures and terminal left-in-place classifications by exact identity.
Carry raw retry identities independently of the initiating host's PathBuf representation so Windows can retry non-UTF-8 files on remote Unix sources.

findings.title: Detached reconciliation still retries failures fixed by a later pass
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/job_record.rs:821 — `LogRead::read_line` adds every `FileFailed` but has no `FileCopied`/`FileSent` removal; `ended_record` then copies that historical union into the settled record.
findings.predicted_failure: A detached job whose retry pass later lands a file still records that file as failed; `jobs retry` can resend or overwrite it, and can retry a run whose terminal failed count is zero.
findings.better_approach: Fold daemon log events in attempt order by `(path, raw)`, remove an identity when it later lands, derive left-in-place only from identities still failed, and refuse reconciliation when the terminal set disagrees with the summary count.

findings.title: Windows controllers lose remote non-UTF-8 retry identities
findings.evidence: crates/blit-cli/src/jobs.rs:403 — `retry_path` reconstructs raw bytes only under `cfg(unix)`; lines 408-410 discard `raw` on Windows and return the lossy display path used to build the remote filter.
findings.predicted_failure: A Windows client retrying a failed non-UTF-8 file on a remote Unix source sends the lossy text in `files_from`; the source matches no file, so the retry may copy nothing and report success.
findings.better_approach: Keep retry identities as text plus raw bytes through orchestration and populate `FilterSpec.files_from_raw` directly, using PathBuf only when enumerating on the actual source host.
